records.question: Is the new rule ending duration of status in effect now?
search_queries: Is the new rule ending duration of status in effect now?
records.answer:
No. According to ISSS, the final rule is not currently in effect. On September 14, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a [preliminary injunction postponing the effective date](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status). The rule will no longer go into effect on September 15, and DHS is barred from implementing it.

**Background:** DHS published the [final rule](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/July/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Publishes-Final-Rule-Eliminating-Duration-of-Status) on July 17, 2026. It would replace D/S with a fixed admission period matching the program length, up to four years. The September 15 effective date was the original schedule, and the court order has since postponed it.

**Current status:** The newest ISSS post I found is the September 14 court-order announcement. It says ISSS is monitoring guidance from DHS, ICE, USCIS, and the Department of State, and will update its guidance as more information becomes available. I didn't find any later ISSS update on this.

Because the situation could change, check with an ISSS advisor if you have travel plans or need to extend your program. ISSS has also published an FAQ page on the final rule in the ISSS Student Portal.
